zoe: Quick follow-up to the RFC on service modularization. I sketched a phased migration approach for contract evolution so we can pay down tech debt without breaking hosted customers. dropping it here for feedback.
matt: Curious — phased how? feature flags or stable adapter layer?
ravi: +1 on adapter layer. Flags are brittle when distributed across dedicated/private deployments.
zoe: Proposal: 3 phases. 1) Interface adapters (compat shims) in front of new modules. 2) Gradual traffic routing by route/model + canary. 3) Deprecation window + cleanup. Keep configs declarative.
amanda: Do we need dual-run mode (old + new) to validate correctness? i.e., shadowing responses for eval.
zoe: Yes shadowing in phase 2. We'll produce diffs and run quality checks tied to existing eval suites.
alex: How do we version contract changes? semantic API versioning or explicit capability flags on routes?
ravi: For internal service boundaries I'd prefer capability flags + explicit schema version on requests. Avoid global semver churn.
matt: Can we see a minimal shim example? how would a router pick compatible variant?
zoe: Example snippet:
```
# router config
routes:
  - path: /generate
    variants:
      - model: gptx-v1
        capabilities: [streaming, tool-calls]
      - model: gptx-v2
        capabilities: [streaming, tool-calls, structured-output]
```
Router picks variant where request.capabilities subset-of variant.capabilities.
amanda: Nice. For Dedicated customers we must ensure no silent fallback unless allowed in their SLA.
zoe: Agreed. Routing policy includes customer_tier guard. No fallback for "locked" customers.
alex: Migration timeline? also who's owning the shims and the compatibility tests?
zoe: Timeline draft: 6 weeks for adapters + infra (phase 1), 4 weeks canary + shadowing (phase 2), 3 months deprecation window (phase 3). Owners: eng-runtime for adapters, eng-platform for router/policies, eng-ml for evals. I'll make a short RACI.
matt: Risks: multiple adapters -> maintenance overhead. Suggest we keep adapter surface minimal and write generator for glue.
ravi: Also watch KV cache semantics — new module must produce identical cache keys or we'll regress perf.
zoe: Good catch. Add cache-key compatibility test to the suite.
amanda: Ops: infra-bot, will you be able to add observability hooks for variant-level latency/cost breakdown?
infra-bot: deploy-bot: observability endpoints can be added. I'll open infra ticket and ensure dashboards for variant-level metrics.
zoe: Action items: (1) zoe to PR adapter design doc by EOD Tue, (2) matt to prototype shim generator, (3) ravi to spec cache-key tests, (4) amanda to draft SLA routing guard. tagging owners here. :thumbsup:
matt: I'll start prototype tomorrow.
ravi: I'll draft tests and link to eval harness.
amanda: I'll write the SLA guard spec and share in #product-security.
zoe: Thanks all. If no blocker I'll post RFC follow-up with timeline and owners tomorrow. :rocket:
